about.title: Etna Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Etna's economy leans on ranching, timber, small manufacturing, and the trades that keep a rural Siskiyou County town running — work that often means machinery, uneven terrain, and long drives between job sites along Main Street or State Route 3. When someone gets hurt on the job here, California's workers' compensation system is usually the first stop, since it's typically the exclusive remedy against an employer no matter who was at fault. But that's not always the whole story: if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate third-party injury claim may be possible alongside comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results — we simply connect injured workers in Etna with an independent attorney who can look at the facts, explain the options plainly, and help sort out whether more than one path applies. There's no cost to start the conversation, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Etna Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Comp vs. Third-Party Line
items.desc: California workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like an equipment maker or another driver can open a separate claim. An independent attorney can help figure out which route, or both, apply to your situation.

items.title: Knowing the Reporting Clock
items.desc: Workers generally have 30 days to report a job injury to their employer to preserve comp eligibility. Missing that window can complicate a claim, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report injuries or file claims. An attorney can help you understand your rights if you feel pressured after speaking up.

items.question: I was hurt on a ranch or farm job outside Etna — does workers' comp still apply?
items.answer: Most California employers are required to carry workers' compensation coverage, including many agricultural operations, though some exemptions and rules can apply. An independent attorney can review your employment situation to clarify your coverage and options.

items.question: Can I file a claim if someone other than my employer caused my injury?
items.answer: Yes — if a third party such as a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the accident, you may be able to pursue a separate injury claim in addition to workers' comp. This is common in construction and equipment-related incidents. A third-party claim generally carries a two-year deadline in California.
